geo-paleo-01-c2.text: U.S. National Park Service. Permineralization and Replacement. National Park Service.
geo-paleo-01-c2.quote: A permineralized fossil is denser and heavier than the original organic material because its pores have been filled by silica or other minerals.
geo-paleo-01-c2.claim: Minerals dissolved in groundwater slowly replace the organic material or fill its pore spaces

geo-paleo-01-c2.text: La Brea Tar Pits and Museum (Natural History Museum of Los Angeles County). La Brea Tar Pits and Hancock Park. tarpits.org.
geo-paleo-01-c2.quote: Over the last 50,000 years, Ice Age animals, plants, and insects were trapped in sticky asphalt, which preserved them for us to find today.
geo-paleo-01-c2.claim: Tar pits (e.g. La Brea, Los Angeles) mire animals in asphalt, preserving their bones.

geo-paleo-01-c3.text: UC Museum of Paleontology, University of California Berkeley. Getting Into the Fossil Record: Focus Questions Key. Understanding Evolution / UCMP, University of California Berkeley.
geo-paleo-01-c3.quote: Soft-bodied organisms are much more likely to decay than organisms with hard body parts such as bones, shells or teeth.
geo-paleo-01-c3.claim: Preservation bias: hard parts survive, so soft-bodied organisms are under-represented.
